blocks.html: Short answer: First time in Bangkok? Lock in three things — an Ayutthaya day trip to the UNESCO ruins, a Damnoen Saduak and Maeklong railway-market tour, and a Chao Phraya dinner cruise. In town, walk the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun yourself, then add a Muay Thai night or a Chinatown street-food tour.

items.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: Bangkok's number-one landmark, home to the Emerald Buddha. Entry is 500 THB, open 8:30 to 15:30; cover shoulders and knees. A guided tour helps the history land.

items.name: Wat Arun & Wat Pho
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A riverside temple pair you can do back to back. Wat Pho has the giant Reclining Buddha; a 3 THB ferry takes you across to Wat Arun's spire. Entry is 200 THB each, best at golden hour.

items.name: Chao Phraya dinner cruise
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A roughly 2-hour evening buffet cruise past a floodlit Wat Arun and Grand Palace, usually with a live band. Several boats rate around 4.5; book online and pick your sailing.

items.name: Damnoen Saduak & Maeklong railway market
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A favourite day trip out of town: a paddleboat ride through Damnoen Saduak floating market, then the Maeklong railway market where vendors fold their awnings each time a train rolls through. Group tours run about 700 to 1,500 THB.

items.name: Ayutthaya UNESCO day trip
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: The old capital, about 1.5 hours from Bangkok. See Wat Mahathat, Wat Chaiwatthanaram and the famous Buddha head in the tree roots; some tours add Bang Pa-In Palace and a boat ride. Half- and full-day options.

items.name: Muay Thai night at Rajadamnern Stadium
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: Live Muay Thai at Rajadamnern, the sport's historic arena. Tickets run from around 1,000 THB for upper seats to 2,000 to 2,500 THB ringside, with the headline bouts later in the evening. Book ahead online.

items.name: Chinatown night street-food tour
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A tuk-tuk crawl through Chinatown after dark, tasting more than five local dishes — seafood, fried noodles, grilled skewers and mango sticky rice to finish. A local guide leads, and some tours pass floodlit temples.

items.name: Amphawa floating market & firefly cruise
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: Amphawa floating market runs Friday to Sunday, afternoon into the evening. Eat your way along the canal, then take a longtail boat to watch fireflies twinkle in the riverside trees after dark. Many tours fold in the Maeklong railway market and hotel transfers.

faq.q: Which activities should I book ahead, and which can I just buy on the day?
faq.a: Book the out-of-town day trips (Ayutthaya, floating markets, Amphawa), the dinner cruise, the food tour and Muay Thai tickets ahead — slots and seats sell out and online prices are usually better. The in-town temples like the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun you can pay for at the gate, no booking needed.

faq.q: What's the difference between Damnoen Saduak and Amphawa — which should I pick?
faq.a: Damnoen Saduak is busiest in the morning and open daily, so it pairs well with the Maeklong railway market as a daytime trip. Amphawa only runs Friday to Sunday, afternoon into the evening, and its draw is the relaxed mood plus the after-dark firefly boat ride. On a weekday pick Damnoen Saduak; if you're here on a weekend and want fireflies, choose Amphawa.

faq.q: How should I dress for Bangkok's temples?
faq.a: Major temples like the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun require shoulders and knees covered — no tank tops, shorts or short skirts. The Grand Palace lends sarongs at the gate if you're underdressed, but the queue is long, so it's easier to arrive covered. Closed-toe or strapped shoes are fine.
